samples.summary: Live slides reader bands table cell bodies but not `data.columnWidths`, leaving the unbounded column allocation the rest of the change caps
samples.evidence: `YorkieSlidesStore.bandElementText` (line 528-543) handles only `shape.text.blocks` and `table.rows[].cells[].body.blocks`. The slides package's shared `bandElementNumerics` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts, `bandTableColumnWidths`) additionally caps a table element's `columnWidths` at MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS and zeroes unusable widths — and the board store (yorkie-board-store.ts:442), the snapshot adapter (`bandSlidesDocumentNumerics`) and the backend PUT (`assertValidTableData`, docs-content.controller.ts:965) all apply it. The live slides store uses its own local walker instead and skips it, so `computeTableLayout` in packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:87-92 still does `new Array(nCols + 1)` and an O(nCols x nRows) loop over a peer-written `columnWidths` of arbitrary length, and a non-finite entry still poisons the running `colX` sum. That is exactly the hung/blank paint the change's own comments cite as the reason for the cap.
searchedFor: checked board store and snapshot adapters for the same call

samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` drops non-finite entries, shifting later columns and able to return an empty array — violating its own documented "may not delete a column" invariant
samples.evidence: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` does `if (ratio === undefined) continue;`, i.e. a non-finite entry is dropped rather than kept as 0. Its own doc comment (lines 243-250) argues at length that the array length *is* `computeTableLayout`'s `numCols` and that shrinking it makes a row's content unreachable (not in the layout, not in `blockParentMap`) — "A band may repair a number; it may not delete a column" — and both other call sites of `normalizeColumnRatio` (numeric-attrs.ts:381 and docs-content.controller.ts:967) deliberately use `?? 0` to preserve indices. Here `cols="1e400"` yields `[]` (asserted by the new test `colsOf('1e400')` -> `[]`), i.e. zero columns, and `cols="1e400,0.5"` shifts column 1 into slot 0.

samples.summary: Backend master band deletes a required `PlaceholderStyle.fontSize`/`lineHeight` where the slides band substitutes a default, storing a master that paints `NaNpx`
samples.evidence: `bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` does `if (banded === undefined) delete style[field];`. `PlaceholderStyle.fontSize`/`lineHeight` are required numbers, which is why the slides-side twin `bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts) explicitly substitutes `DEFAULT_MASTER.placeholderStyles[...]` instead, with the comment '`undefined` would paint `NaNpx` in the hint and store an undefined size in the seeded block'. A PUT carrying `fontSize: 0` or `-1` therefore *stores* a master with the field missing; readers that do not run `bandMasterNumerics` (backend/CLI export paths, `seedPlaceholderBlocks` fed from the stored value) get `undefined` where a number is required.

samples.summary: `bandBlockNumerics` rewrites a numeric-string `listLevel` to 0, destroying list nesting the PPTX exporter was explicitly written to coerce
samples.evidence: `block.listLevel = normalizeListLevel(asFiniteNumber(block.listLevel))` — `asFiniteNumber` rejects anything that is not `typeof 'number'`, so a stored `listLevel: "2"` becomes 0. The same change's `listLevelAttr` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts) documents that a string level is a real stored shape ('the v1 content PUT never looks at `listLevel`, so `{"type":"list-item","listLevel":"2"}` is stored as the *string* it was sent as') and keeps a `Number(...)` coercion so it exports at its real level. Since the frontend export reads through `YorkieSlidesStore.read()`, which now bands first, the coercion can no longer see the string — the deck silently flattens to level 0.

samples.summary: A user-specified row height is silently discarded when any cell in that row has non-finite content geometry
samples.evidence: Step 5b runs `if (userHeight !== undefined && userHeight > rowHeights[r])`, but at that point `rowHeights[r]` is `NaN` for a row containing a cell whose content height came out non-finite (step 4 does `Math.max(NaN, …)`), and every comparison against `NaN` is false — so the user's dragged height is skipped. Step 5d then only re-derives the row from the repaired *cell content* (line 404-410, `derived = MIN_ROW_HEIGHT` maxed with cell heights), never consulting `tableData.rowHeights` again. The dragged minimum is therefore lost rather than restored.

samples.summary: Step 5d repairs a `rowSpan > 1` cell's height but does not re-derive the rows it spans, leaving repaired content taller than the published row geometry
samples.evidence: `bandCellGeometry` repairs the anchor cell of a `rowSpan > 1` merge, but the row re-derivation immediately below is skipped (`if (Number.isFinite(rowHeights[r]) && rowHeights[r] > 0) continue;`) whenever the spanned rows happened to stay finite — which step 5d's own comment says is the normal case for a poisoned merged cell, since step 4's `rowSpan === 1` pass skips it and `cell.height > spannedHeight` is false for `NaN`. The repaired cell then paints/hit-tests taller than `rowYOffsets` allows for.

verdict.reason: The live slides reader's local walker `YorkieSlidesStore.bandElementText` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:528-543, called from readElement:638) bands only shape `text.blocks` and table `rows[].cells[].body.blocks`; it never touches `data.columnWidths`, and the store does not import `bandElementNumerics` (imports, lines 41-68). The shared cap exists and is applied by every sibling reader — board store (yorkie-board-store.ts:442), snapshot adapters (snapshot-adapters.ts:53,75 → band-numerics.ts:216), backend PUT (docs-content.controller.ts:966) — via `bandTableColumnWidths` (band-numerics.ts:72-77, slice to MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS + non-finite → 0). Nothing else on the live path supplies it: `migrateDocument`/`migrateElement` (migrate.ts:77-211) pass non-shape elements through unchanged, and the slides views (slides-view.tsx:688, mobile-slides-view.tsx:156) consume `store.read()` with no post-band. The sink is unguarded: computeTableLayout (table-renderer.ts:86-92) allocates `new Array(nCols + 1)` from the raw array length, runs O(nCols x nRows) loops (96-133), and accumulates `colX` as a running sum so one non-finite entry poisons every later boundary; the only clamps there are on gridSpan/rowSpan. The store's write path also checks only length equality (updateTableColumnWidths:2617-2640), and the store's band tests (yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:897) cover bodies/notes but not columnWidths. Real and blocking under the correctness lens: a peer-written columnWidths of arbitrary length or containing NaN/Infinity produces a hung or blank paint for every other live viewer — exactly the failure the twin cap elsewhere prevents. Severity major.
